why: The graph's connected components are what matter, and for each one you only need its smallest and largest label. Union-find merges components edge by edge and keeps a running min and max at each root, so the answer is the largest max - min over the roots.
hints: You never need a component's full list of nodes. What two numbers per component are enough?
Keep min and max at each union-find root; when two roots merge, the new root takes the smaller min and the larger max.
Initialise min = max = label for nodes 1..g_nodes, union every edge, then scan the roots for the largest max - min. O((n + m) alpha(n)).
pitfalls: Isolated nodes are components with difference 0; the answer is at least 0.
Nodes are labeled 1..g_nodes, so size arrays g_nodes + 1.
Use iterative find: 10^5 nodes in a chain would overflow recursion.
constraints:
• 1 ≤ g_nodes ≤ 105
  • 1 ≤ g_edges ≤ min(105, g_nodes × (g_nodes − 1) / 2)
  • 1 ≤ g_from[i], g_to[i] ≤ g_nodes
